name: Lourdes Marcano
bio:
I am a physicist and materials scientist at the University of Oviedo, working at the intersection of nanomagnetism, bioinspired materials and biomedical function. My research began with magnetotactic bacteria: living systems that build remarkably precise magnetic crystals and organise them into nanoscale compasses. These magnetosomes became a way to ask how composition, shape and organisation govern magnetic behaviour.

Through research at UPV/EHU, HZB/BESSY II and CIC biomaGUNE, I developed approaches that combine synchrotron and neutron characterisation with magnetic measurements and materials design. Today, I lead an independent research line connecting naturally formed and engineered magnetic nanomaterials with diagnostic imaging and thermal therapies. My current interests focus on iron oxides and on understanding how their microscopic structure controls the interactions between light, magnetism and heat—from defects and doping to energy conversion and transport.

publications.title: Protein-Engineered Iron Nanoclusters as Hybrid Theranostic Materials for MRI Monitoring and Treatment of Cardiac Fibrosis
publications.summary: Protein-engineered iron nanoclusters combine positive MRI contrast with antifibrotic activity. Tests in a three-dimensional human cardiac tissue model explore a hybrid platform for monitoring and treating fibrosis.
publications.image_alt: Graphical abstract for Protein-Engineered Iron Nanoclusters as Hybrid Theranostic Materials for MRI Monitoring and Treatment of Cardiac Fibrosis
publications.image_rights: Author-provided original artwork; author-authorised use on personal scientific website

publications.title: Extending Field Limits in Nanoscale Magnetic Imaging With Metamaterial‐Inspired Magnetic Flux Concentrators
publications.summary: Metamaterial-inspired flux concentrators amplify magnetic fields locally. This extends the operating range of nanoscale magnetic imaging without increasing the field applied by the instrument.
publications.image_alt: Figure 1 for Extending Field Limits in Nanoscale Magnetic Imaging With Metamaterial‐Inspired Magnetic Flux Concentrators
publications.image_credit: Barrera et al. · Small, 2026 · CC BY 4.0.

publications.title: Mn-ferrite nanoparticles as multifunctional probes for tri-modal photothermal, magnetic, and colorimetric paper-based biosensors
publications.summary: Mn-ferrite nanoparticles bring photothermal, magnetic and colorimetric responses into one material platform. Their multifunctionality opens routes to paper-based biosensing.

publications.title: Exploring the Complex Interplay of Anisotropies in Magnetosomes of Magnetotactic Bacteria
publications.summary: Magnetosome behaviour emerges from several competing sources of magnetic anisotropy. Resolving their interplay helps explain how individual crystals and their chain arrangement shape the response of magnetic bacteria.
publications.image_alt: Graphical abstract for Exploring the Complex Interplay of Anisotropies in Magnetosomes of Magnetotactic Bacteria

publications.title: Magnetic vector tomography reveals giant magnetofossils are optimised for magnetointensity reception
publications.summary: Three-dimensional magnetic vector tomography reveals how giant magnetofossils respond to magnetic-field intensity. Their unusual shapes provide a window into biological magnetic sensing.
publications.image_alt: Figure 1 for Magnetic vector tomography reveals giant magnetofossils are optimised for magnetointensity reception
publications.image_credit: Harrison et al. · Communications Earth & Environment, 2025 · CC BY 4.0.

publications.title: Micromagnetic structure of oxidized magnetite nanoparticles: sharp structural versus diffuse magnetic interface
publications.summary: Oxidation creates a sharp structural boundary but a diffuse magnetic interface in magnetite nanoparticles. The distinction shows why a structural core–shell picture alone cannot describe their magnetic response.

publications.title: Proximity effects, exchange bias and magnetic relaxation in γ-Fe 2 O 3 nanoparticles
publications.summary: The study connects proximity effects, exchange bias and magnetic relaxation in maghemite nanoparticles. It examines how nanoscale structure and interparticle environments influence magnetic behaviour.

publications.title: Determining the Magnetic Anisotropy at the Nanoscale by Means of X-ray Magnetic-sensitive and Element-selective Microscopy Methods
publications.summary: This chapter explains how magnetic-sensitive, element-selective X-ray microscopy measures anisotropy at the nanoscale. It brings together experimental approaches for studying individual magnetic objects.

publications.title: Magnetochrome-catalyzed oxidation of ferrous iron by MamP enables magnetite crystal growth in the magnetotactic bacterium AMB-1
publications.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
publications.summary: The magnetochrome protein MamP catalyses ferrous-iron oxidation during magnetite crystal growth. This identifies a molecular step linking biological iron chemistry to magnetic biomineralisation.
publications.image_alt: Figure 1 for Magnetochrome-catalyzed oxidation of ferrous iron by MamP enables magnetite crystal growth in the magnetotactic bacterium AMB-1
publications.image_credit: Amor et al. · PNAS, 2024 · CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

publications.title: Size-Dependence and High Temperature Stability of Radial Vortex Magnetic Textures Imprinted by Superconductor Stray Fields
publications.summary: Superconductor stray fields imprint radial vortex textures in a magnetic layer. The work examines how their size and thermal stability govern the persistence of these unusual magnetic states.
publications.image_alt: Graphical abstract for Size-Dependence and High Temperature Stability of Radial Vortex Magnetic Textures Imprinted by Superconductor Stray Fields

publications.title: Incorporation of Tb and Gd improves the diagnostic functionality of magnetotactic bacteria
publications.summary: Introducing Tb and Gd adds diagnostic functions to magnetotactic bacteria. In vitro tests demonstrate fluorescence and dual MRI contrast, expanding the capabilities of a naturally magnetic biological platform.

publications.title: Tuning the Magnetic Response of Magnetospirillum magneticum by Changing the Culture Medium: A Straightforward Approach to Improve Their Hyperthermia Efficiency
publications.summary: Changing bacterial culture conditions tunes the magnetic response of Magnetospirillum magneticum. This provides a biological route to improving magnetic-hyperthermia performance.
publications.image_alt: Graphical abstract for Tuning the Magnetic Response of Magnetospirillum magneticum by Changing the Culture Medium: A Straightforward Approach to Improve Their Hyperthermia Efficiency

publications.title: Extremely long-range, high-temperature Josephson coupling across a half-metallic ferromagnet
publications.summary: Josephson coupling persists across unexpectedly long distances in a half-metallic ferromagnet. The finding connects magnetic interfaces and superconducting transport in complex oxides.
publications.image_alt: Figure 1 for Extremely long-range, high-temperature Josephson coupling across a half-metallic ferromagnet
publications.image_credit: Sanchez-Manzano et al. · First published in Nature Materials, 2022. Author reuse.

publications.title: Magnetic Anisotropy of Individual Nanomagnets Embedded in Biological Systems Determined by Axi-asymmetric X-ray Transmission Microscopy
publications.summary: A magnetic X-ray microscopy method determines the anisotropy of individual nanomagnets inside biological systems. It moves beyond ensemble averages to reveal the behaviour of nanoparticles in their native environment.
publications.image_alt: Graphical abstract for Magnetic Anisotropy of Individual Nanomagnets Embedded in Biological Systems Determined by Axi-asymmetric X-ray Transmission Microscopy

publications.title: Modifying the magnetic response of magnetotactic bacteria: incorporation of Gd and Tb ions into the magnetosome structure
publications.summary: Gd and Tb can be incorporated into magnetosome structures to modify their magnetic response. The work explores how biological synthesis can be extended through controlled chemical modification.
publications.image_alt: Cover illustration for Modifying the magnetic response of magnetotactic bacteria: incorporation of Gd and Tb ions into the magnetosome structure
publications.image_credit: Jefremovas et al. · Royal Society of Chemistry, 2022. Author reuse.

publications.title: Strain tuning of Néel temperature in YCrO3 epitaxial thin films
publications.summary: Epitaxial strain tunes the Néel temperature of YCrO₃ thin films. The result links lattice deformation to antiferromagnetic ordering in an oxide material.

publications.title: Towards the design of contrast-enhanced agents: systematic Ga 3+ doping on magnetite nanoparticles
publications.summary: Systematic Ga³⁺ doping connects magnetite composition with magnetic and MRI-relevant properties. This provides a materials-design framework for contrast-enhanced agents.

publications.title: A Milestone in the Chemical Synthesis of Fe 3 O 4 Nanoparticles: Unreported Bulklike Properties Lead to a Remarkable Magnetic Hyperthermia
publications.summary: Chemically synthesised magnetite nanoparticles display exceptionally bulk-like magnetic properties. Their strong magnetic-hyperthermia response links crystal quality to energy dissipation.
publications.image_alt: Graphical abstract for A Milestone in the Chemical Synthesis of Fe 3 O 4 Nanoparticles: Unreported Bulklike Properties Lead to a Remarkable Magnetic Hyperthermia

publications.title: Nanoflowers Versus Magnetosomes: Comparison Between Two Promising Candidates for Magnetic Hyperthermia Therapy
publications.summary: A comparison of nanoflowers and magnetosomes examines two different routes to magnetic heating. The study relates their architecture and magnetic response to hyperthermia performance.

publications.title: Nature Driven Magnetic Nanoarchitectures
publications.summary: This chapter follows magnetosome formation, chain magnetism and biomedical applications. It presents natural magnetic nanoarchitectures as both physical model systems and functional materials.

publications.title: Nonreciprocal Transport in a Rashba Ferromagnet, Delafossite PdCoO2
publications.summary: The study reveals nonreciprocal transport in the Rashba ferromagnet PdCoO₂. It explores how broken symmetries and spin–orbit interactions shape charge transport.
publications.image_alt: Graphical abstract for Nonreciprocal Transport in a Rashba Ferromagnet, Delafossite PdCoO2

publications.title: Shaping Up Zn-Doped Magnetite Nanoparticles from Mono- and Bimetallic Oleates: The Impact of Zn Content, Fe Vacancies, and Morphology on Magnetic Hyperthermia Performance
publications.summary: Tailoring Zn content, iron vacancies and particle morphology controls the heating performance of magnetite nanoparticles. The study connects detailed local chemistry with effective magnetic energy conversion.
publications.image_alt: Graphical abstract for Shaping Up Zn-Doped Magnetite Nanoparticles from Mono- and Bimetallic Oleates: The Impact of Zn Content, Fe Vacancies, and Morphology on Magnetic Hyperthermia Performance

publications.title: Controlled Magnetic Anisotropy in Single Domain Mn-doped Biosynthesized Nanoparticles
publications.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
publications.summary: Mn doping offers control over the magnetic anisotropy of biosynthesised single-domain nanoparticles. The result uses biological crystals as a platform for tuning a fundamental magnetic property.
publications.image_alt: Graphical abstract for Controlled Magnetic Anisotropy in Single Domain Mn-doped Biosynthesized Nanoparticles

publications.title: Elucidating the role of shape anisotropy in faceted magnetic nanoparticles using biogenic magnetosomes as a model
publications.summary: Biogenic magnetosomes serve as precise model particles for separating shape anisotropy from other magnetic contributions. Their faceted morphology exposes how crystal geometry controls nanoscale magnetism.

publications.title: Magnetosomes could be protective shields against metal stress in magnetotactic bacteria
publications.summary: Magnetosomes may contribute to the response of magnetic bacteria to metal stress. The work investigates a biological role for magnetic biomineralisation beyond navigation.

publications.title: Probing the stability and magnetic properties of magnetosome chains in freeze-dried magnetotactic bacteria
publications.summary: Freeze-dried bacteria provide a way to examine the stability of magnetosome chains. The study tests how preservation affects this natural magnetic architecture and its properties.

publications.title: Mn-Doping level dependence on the magnetic response of Mn x Fe 3−x O 4 ferrite nanoparticles
publications.summary: The magnetic response of ferrite nanoparticles changes with Mn-doping level. The work connects composition to nanoscale magnetic behaviour across a controlled series of materials.

publications.title: Using the singular value decomposition to extract 2D correlation functions from scattering patterns
publications.journal: Acta Crystallographica Section A Foundations and Advances
publications.summary: Singular value decomposition extracts two-dimensional correlation functions from scattering patterns. This analytical approach helps recover structural information encoded in anisotropic scattering.

publications.title: Configuration of the magnetosome chain: a natural magnetic nanoarchitecture
publications.summary: Magnetosome chains form a natural one-dimensional magnetic nanoarchitecture. The study connects the arrangement of individual crystals with the collective magnetic response of the chain.
publications.image_alt: Cover illustration for Configuration of the magnetosome chain: a natural magnetic nanoarchitecture
publications.image_credit: Orue et al. · Royal Society of Chemistry, 2018. Author reuse.

publications.title: Magnetic Study of Co-Doped Magnetosome Chains
publications.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry C
publications.summary: Co doping modifies the magnetic properties of magnetosome chains. Combining biological synthesis and magnetic characterisation clarifies how composition and chain architecture work together.

publications.title: Influence of the bacterial growth phase on the magnetic properties of magnetosomes synthesized by Magnetospirillum gryphiswaldense
publications.journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - General Subjects
publications.summary: The bacterial growth phase influences the magnetic properties of biosynthesised magnetosomes. This establishes a connection between biological development and the physical response of magnetic crystals.

publications.title: On the mineral core of ferritin-like proteins: structural and magnetic characterization
publications.summary: Structural and magnetic characterisation probes the mineral cores of ferritin-like proteins. These confined biological iron systems connect biomineralisation with nanoscale materials physics.

publications.title: Studying nanoparticles’ 3D shape by aspect maps: Determination of the morphology of bacterial magnetic nanoparticles
publications.summary: Aspect maps recover three-dimensional particle morphology from complementary views. Applied to bacterial magnetic nanoparticles, they connect crystal shape with quantitative nanoscale characterisation.

publications.title: Fe45Ni55 Magnetic Nanoparticles Obtained by Electric Explosion of Wire for the Development of Functional Composites
publications.summary: Electrical wire explosion produces Fe–Ni magnetic nanoparticles for functional composites. The study characterises a physical synthesis route to magnetic filler materials.

publications.title: Tailoring functional properties of Ni nanoparticles-acrylic copolymer composites with different concentrations of magnetic filler
publications.summary: Changing the concentration and aggregation of Ni nanoparticles tunes acrylic-composite magnetic properties. The work connects filler organisation with static and microwave response.

projects.title: Biological and bioinspired magnetic micro- and nanostructures for personalised theranostic interventions
projects.funder: Spanish State Research Agency · Consolidación Investigadora 2025
projects.question: How can biological and bioinspired magnetic architectures bring diagnosis and intervention together?
projects.summary: Developing micro- and nanostructures whose composition, organisation and magnetic response can be tailored for theranostic applications.
objectives: Design biological and bioinspired magnetic architectures.
Connect material properties with diagnostic and therapeutic functionality.

projects.title: Unconventional magnetic nanostructures as thermal agents for medical applications
projects.funder: Spanish State Research Agency · Knowledge Generation 2023
projects.question: How does magnetic nanoarchitecture determine the conversion of external stimuli into heat?
projects.summary: Investigating unconventional magnetic nanostructures as thermal agents, connecting materials design with magnetic and photothermal response.
objectives: Relate structural and magnetic properties to thermal performance.

projects.title: Eco-friendly and bioinspired protein-based synthesis of magnetic nanomaterials for advanced cancer theranostics
projects.funder: European Commission · Marie Skłodowska-Curie Postdoctoral Fellowship
projects.question: Can engineered proteins guide sustainable synthesis of magnetic materials for theranostics?
projects.summary: An individual fellowship at CIC biomaGUNE linking protein engineering, bioinspired magnetic-material synthesis and biomedical characterisation.
objectives: Use engineered proteins as templates for magnetic nanomaterials.

projects.title: Bioinspired magnetic materials for biomedical applications
projects.question: What can biological synthesis teach us about the design of functional magnetic nanomaterials?
projects.summary: Competitive seed funding to establish an independent research line in bioinspired magnetic materials at the University of Oviedo.
objectives: Explore biological and bioinspired routes to magnetic materials.
Develop the materials foundations for biomedical functionality.

projects.title: Magnetotactic bacteria as biological nanorobots
projects.question: Can naturally magnetic bacteria become controllable platforms for thermal interventions?
projects.summary: An individual Leonardo Fellowship investigating magnetotactic bacteria as biological nanorobots and exploring their response to magnetic and photothermal stimuli.
objectives: Study magnetic bacteria as bioinspired functional platforms.
Explore their potential for combined thermal approaches.
